unitemized.reason: This is the negative side of vf-063. The positive 'not verified' items for the absent-spec case already cover it, and 'treated as clean' has no separate observable form.
It only applies when a requirement 'appears unimplemented', which is the agent's own judgement. No predicate in the reference language can observe that.
It has the same unobservable condition as vf-070: the requirement 'appears unimplemented'.
It only applies when the removed behavior is 'still present', which is a judgement about the code. No predicate can express it.
It has the same unobservable condition as vf-076: the behavior is still present.
It only applies to a RENAMED entry whose TO name is not also under MODIFIED. The reference language cannot express that condition, and an unconditional read of the main spec would be wrong.
It only applies when the renamed behavior 'appears unimplemented', which is the agent's judgement and not observable.
It has the same unobservable condition as vf-084.
It only applies when the baseline requirement for a RENAMED entry cannot be found or read. That depends on each entry and cannot be expressed as a predicate.
It only applies to a removal- or rename-only change (REMOVED/RENAMED requirements present, no ADDED/MODIFIED). No predicate can tell which delta sections hold requirements.
It has the same unexpressible removal- or rename-only condition as vf-088.
It only applies when a delta spec has no parseable requirements. No predicate in the reference language can observe that.
